agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager would read this as the usual teacher-to-trainer letter: it relies on transferable habits rather than proof such as audited signed records or the 20-to-12-hour training redesign, so it probably won't get a phone screen.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim and states the GMP and LMS gaps plainly, but it adds things the brief doesn't support: 'moved my courses fully onto Google Classroom', 'learn new systems quickly' and adapting training to different experience levels.

works_the_facts.reason: Figures are restated without being worked: there's no 40% cut from 20 to 12 hours, no total of roughly 18 teachers trained, no estimate of roughly 1,000 students without a serious injury, and the 41-to-58% gain isn't framed as a 17-point rise.

right_comparison.reason: Only the AP pass rate gets a before and after; the 20-hour training it replaced is left out, and there's no comparison with a candidate who already has GMP experience.

qualification.reason: The gap is admitted with only a vague promise to learn, when the GMP course ending May 2 and the June 14 start date would have given dated, checkable conditions.

objections.reason: It names the regulated-industry objection but answers with soft habits, leaving out the facts that answer it directly: signed training records for every trainee and two state audits that found nothing.

fit.reason: It's a one-page cover letter as asked, but it uses placeholders for the name, company and hiring manager (Laura Benitez, Calder Pharmaceuticals, Karen Doyle) even though those were known, and it leaves out availability for interviews.
